questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always wanted to visit Australia. It was a coincidence that I got to live in Melbourne, but I am so glad I did. Best city ever!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Best experience I ever had

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The process is very difficult and complex

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Stop 1 was a huge help. 
The exchange intro was also very good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is so hard to find housing. The demand is much higher than the supply which also means that the cost is very expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend it because it is so nice to get the real experience of living in the city, and I really enjoyed having roomies so I didn't feel lonely. But it is important to know that it is very expensive and the process is very tough and frustrating. But it is so for everyone - so don't give up! You will find something eventually.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is very complex and difficult to figure out. There are so many things you have to get done. But the University was so helpful and they replied very fast to all my questions, which was so nice!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
At the beginning of my semester, I wanted to change one of my subjects. I contacted stop 1 to ask for help and they were very helpful. I had to contact the teacher/professor of the subject to ask for permission, and he answered so fast and was very sweet. Overall, it was successful! 
It is nice to know that you don't have to have all your subjects figured out and fixed before you arrived. You have time to solve things and get the help you need during the intro of the exchange. Relax and don't worry!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for all the help you need - no matter what it concerns - you will get it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of courses was very high. Way higher than I expected it would be.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Patent law 
Principle of Business Law 
Corporate Law 
Legal Language

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose BA courses and make it as easy for yourself as possible. It takes time to get used to the legal system in Australia, to study in another language, and how things work at the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Heaps of social clubs and activities were available for the students at the university. We were introduced to all of them during the intro of the semester, which was very nice! I joined different kinds of clubs, which I highly recommend because it made it way more easy to get new friends - both other exchange students and other locals too.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the surf club, the diving club, the mountaineering club, and the dance club. I highly recommend the surf club. The committee was so nice and I got to know so many new people at the parties at Tikki House. The surf camp itself was also so much fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Experience Melbourne - the city is amazing! 
During the holidays I traveled around Australia. The country is amazing to travel in and there are so many incredible things to see and places to visit!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Everyone is so nice and friendly and easy to talk to. I felt very much at home in the city already from the beginning!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the social clubs! It is definitely the best way to get to know local students. People in Australia are so friendly and welcoming, so they are easy to talk to and make you feel a part of the community.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No cultural differences were particularly challenging. Of course, there are cultural differences, but I was curious and wanted to get to know all those differences. I think it is a part of being on exchange, so I just enjoyed getting to know them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way of living in Australia. The way people think and meet each other. It is very inspiring and I want to take it with me home.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make it easy for yourself when choosing the subjects! 
2. Find housing with roommates so you don't get to live by yourself. 
3. Join the social clubs so you get invited to house parties and get to know local students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find housing close to the university. The location of Unimelb Parkville is very good, so if you get to live close by, you know that you live in a good location close to all the good places and things of the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I am forever thankful for this experience. It was very special to get a close connection to Melbourne itself and share the experience with all the wonderful people I met during the semester.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you are far away from home from all your friends and your family. You are going to live a separate life with only new people, which can feel a bit lonely sometimes. Even though I had the time of my life in Australia, I was surprised at how rarely I was in contact with people at home. I talked to a lot of my exchange friends about this during the semester, and they all felt the same. So it is a common thing being on exchange, which is nice to know beforehand.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy the time of your life!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
